articles.title: Context-specific effects of CCM2 on atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Genetic variants in the Cerebral Cavernous Malformation 2 ( CCM2 ) locus are associated with coronary artery disease (CAD), but the role of CCM2 in atherosclerosis is unknown. We previously identified CCM2 through endothelial cell (EC) Perturb-seq as a regulator of transcriptional programs enriched for CAD risk genes, and predicted that reduced CCM2 function would be athero-protective. Here, we integrated human genetics, functional studies in human aortic ECs, and single cell profiling with mouse models of atherosclerosis to define the effects of reduced CCM2 signaling across disease stages. Ccm2 +/- mice developed less atherosclerosis after 12 weeks of high-fat, high-cholesterol diet. At baseline, aortic ECs from Ccm2 +/- mice exhibited reduced inflammatory transcriptional programs, and CCM2 knockout in human aortic ECs increased KLF2 expression and reduced monocyte adhesion and procoagulant activity. However, this protective phenotype was not sustained during disease progression. After 12 weeks of high-fat, high-cholesterol diet, Ccm2 +/- mice exhibited increased circulating TNFα and increased inflammatory programs in aortic ECs and T cells. Consistent with this transition, Ccm2 +/- showed increased atherosclerotic burden after 20 weeks of atherogenic diet. Human genetic analyses showed a similar context-dependent association. The lead variant in the CCM2 locus (rs2107732, a missense V53I coding variant in CCM2 ) was associated with lower CAD risk in the general population but higher CAD risk in clinical trial cohorts enriched for cardiometabolic disease. These results demonstrate how the phenotypic consequences of a CAD-associated gene can depend on disease context and stage.
ONE SENTENCE SUMMARY: CCM2 heterozygosity reduces endothelial inflammation and early atherosclerosis but worsens late-stage disease, consistent with human genetics.

articles.title: An endothelial-specific TIE2-L914F mouse model reveals cellular mechanisms of venous malformation progression and recapitulates the patients' response to targeted therapy.
articles.abstract: TIE2 p.L914F is the most common driver mutation of sporadic venous malformation (VM), a disease characterized by massively enlarged veins. The study of the molecular and cellular mechanisms contributing to TIE2-driven VM has been hindered by the lack of a genetic in vivo model. We generated a mouse system in which TIE2 L914F is expressed postnatally in endothelial cells (EC). Mutant mice develop visible lesions with dilated veins with irregular smooth muscle cell coverage, histologically mimicking patients' VM. With the use of an mCherry reporter we demonstrate that lesions form within the venous vasculature, and mutant ECs undergo clonal expansion fueled by a biphasic mechanism consisting of an early burst of proliferation followed by cell size increase. Targeted treatment with rapamycin partially reduces lesion growth by targeting increased proliferation and prolongs mouse survival, demonstrating this genetic murine model recapitulates the patients' therapeutic response. Together, these findings provide new cellular and mechanistic insights into TIE2 p.L914F-driven venous malformation and establish a genetic platform for preclinical therapeutic studies.

articles.title: Lymphatic Malformation Involving Cavernous Sinus With Sellar Extension: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Lymphatic malformations are benign vascular anomalies that most commonly occur in the head and neck region during childhood, and primary intracranial involvement is extremely rare. Lesions involving the cavernous sinus are particularly unusual, given the absence of well-established lymphatic structures in this region. The authors report the case of a 63-year-old man who presented with headache, ptosis, and diplopia. Imaging revealed a homogeneously enhancing mass involving the right cavernous sinus. Partial resection was performed via an endoscopic trans-sphenoidal approach. Histopathological examination demonstrated dilated thin-walled vascular channels lined by endothelial cells with immunoreactivity for podoplanin, suggesting lymphatic endothelial differentiation. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of cavernous sinus lesions and underscores the importance of careful clinicopathological correlation and consideration of a broad differential diagnosis, including lymphatic and other vascular malformations.

articles.title: De novo brain arteriovenous malformation after tumor resection: case report and literature review.
articles.abstract: The congenital origin of brain arteriovenous malformations (bAVMs) has been increasingly challenged by reports of de novo bAVMs in patients previously confirmed to have no vascular malformation. We describe the oldest patient reported in the English language literature harboring a de novo bAVM. An uneventful frontal convexity meningioma resection was performed for a 60-year-old woman, and at 67 years of age, a bAVM was detected by MRI and confirmed by digital subtraction angiography at the site of the previous meningioma resection. This case adds to the growing literature that the etiology of bAVMs is most likely multifactorial.

articles.title: Gamma knife surgery with and without embolization for cerebral arteriovenous malformations: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: The benefit and risk of gamma knife surgery (GKS) in the treatment of residual cerebral arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) after endovascular embolization remain controversial. The aim of this meta-analysis was to assess current evidence regarding the efficiency and safety of GKS for AVMs with and without prior embolization. To compare GKS in patients with and without embolization, the authors conducted a meta-analysis of studies by searching the literature via PubMed and EMBASE databases for the period between January 2006 and December 2017. Six retrospective studies were finally identified. Outcomes were the rate of AVM obliteration on a 3-year follow-up angiogram, hemorrhage at 3 years after GKS and permanent neurological deficits. Six studies eligible for analysis included 2069 patients: 637 had undergone embolization followed by GKS, and 1432 had undergone GKS alone. The obliteration rate was significantly lower in patients who had undergone embolization followed by GKS than in those who had undergone GKS alone (49.5% vs 70.4%, OR 2.29, 95% CI 1.55-3.38, p < 0.00001). Subgroup analysis also indicated high obliteration rates in 'similar mean nidus volume', 'high quality' and 'sample size over 100 patients' subgroups. However, the rates of rehemorrhage (8.9% vs 4.2%, OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.23-1.57, p = 0.29) and permanent neurological deficits rate (3.6% vs 4.6%, OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.57-3.12, p = 0.51) were not significantly different between the two groups and subgroups. Embolization prior to GKS significantly decreases the AVM obliteration rate and didn't reduce the risk of hemorrhage and permanent neurological deficits. Further evaluation by well-designed prospective or randomized cohort studies is highly needed.

articles.title: Hemodynamics Associated With Intracerebral Arteriovenous Malformations: The Effects of Treatment Modalities.
articles.abstract: The understanding of the physiology of cerebral arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) continues to expand. Knowledge of the hemodynamics of blood flow associated with AVMs is also progressing as imaging and treatment modalities advance. The authors present a comprehensive literature review that reveals the physical hemodynamics of AVMs, and the effect that various treatment modalities have on AVM hemodynamics and the surrounding cortex and vasculature. The authors discuss feeding arteries, flow through the nidus, venous outflow, and the relative effects of radiosurgical monotherapy, endovascular embolization alone, and combined microsurgical treatments. The hemodynamics associated with intracranial AVMs is complex and likely changes over time with changes in the physical morphology and angioarchitecture of the lesions. Hemodynamic change may be even more of a factor as it pertains to the vast array of single and multimodal treatment options available. An understanding of AVM hemodynamics associated with differing treatment modalities can affect treatment strategies and should be considered for optimal clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Treatment Outcomes of A Randomized Trial of Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformation-Eligible Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformation Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The guideline for treating unruptured brain arteriovenous malformations (ubAVMs) remains controversial. A Randomized Trial of Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations (ARUBA) reported lower risk of stroke or death with conservative management compared to interventional treatment. There were numerous limitations to the study, including short follow-up period and disproportionate number of patients treated with surgery and embolization.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether treatment of ARUBA-eligible patients have acceptable outcomes at our institution.
METHODS: Retrospective analysis was performed on 673 patients with brain AVMs treated at our institution between 2001 and 2014. One hundred five patients were ARUBA eligible and included in the study. Patients were divided into the microsurgery or Gamma Knife Radiosurgery (GKS; Elekta, Stockholm, Sweden) arm depending on their final treatment. Mean follow-up period was 43 mo (range 4-136 mo). Primary outcome was stroke or death.
RESULTS: A total of 8 (7.6%) patients had a stroke or died. The overall risk of stroke or death was 11.4% (5 of 44 patients) for the microsurgery arm and 4.9% (3 of 61 patients) for the GKS arm. The annual rates of stroke or death were 2.1%, 4.0%, and 1.2% for the entire patient cohort, microsurgery arm, and GKS arm, respectively. AVM obliteration rates at the end of the follow-up period were 95.5% and 47.5% for the microsurgery and GKS arms, respectively.
CONCLUSION: We report a lower overall risk of stroke or death in our ARUBA-eligible patients following treatment than ARUBA. Our results suggest that microsurgery and GKS may be appropriate treatments for patients with ubAVM.

articles.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Induced Cardiovascular Disease: The Role of Accelerated Senescence in Vascular Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
SIGNIFICANCE: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy by reactivating antitumor immunity and improving outcomes across multiple malignancies. Yet, clinical observations and preclinical studies suggest that ICIs may increase long-term cardiovascular disease risk, including hypertension, atherosclerosis, and thrombosis. The underlying mechanisms remain incompletely defined, highlighting the need for focused investigation into the vascular consequences of immune activation.
RECENT ADVANCES: ICI-induced immune activation disrupts vascular and immune homeostasis through persistent production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial dysfunction, and accumulation of cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Sustained T-cell activation enhances ROS generation, driving DNA damage and senescence in both endothelial and immune cells. ICIs may also promote endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndoMT) through chronic oxidative and inflammatory signaling, contributing to fibrosis, vascular stiffness, and chronic inflammation. Transforming growth factor-beta, although immunosuppressive in many contexts, can drive profibrotic and EndoMT programs within the vasculature. Other cytokines and regulators, including interleukin-17 and regulator of calcineurin 1, have been implicated in vascular remodeling, atherosclerosis, and hypertension.
CRITICAL ISSUES: The relative roles of ROS, mitochondrial dysfunction, cfDNA-driven inflammation, and EndoMT in ICI-associated vascular senescence remain unclear. While inflammation-induced vascular damage is well-recognized, direct ICI-specific mechanisms require stronger evidence. How senescent endothelial and immune cells influence therapy resistance and remodeling of the tumor microenvironment also remains to be defined.
FUTURE DIRECTIONS: Mitochondrial and cytosolic ROS sources-arising from electron leakage during oxidative phosphorylation and NADPH oxidases activity-shape immune signaling and sustain T-cell activation during checkpoint blockade. The DNA damage response kinases ataxia-telangiectasia mutated and ATM- and Rad3-related, activated by oxidative and replicative stress, engage p53-dependent senescence pathways in endothelial and immune cells. Future studies should evaluate biomarkers such as cfDNA and thrombospondin-1 and explore senescence-targeting or redox-modulating interventions that may alleviate cardiovascular toxicity without diminishing antitumor efficacy. This review outlines mechanistic pathways linking ICIs to vascular dysfunction and senescence, integrating preclinical data with emerging clinical insights. It distinguishes established processes from ICI-specific hypotheses and identifies key gaps requiring clinical validation. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 45, 821-839.

articles.title: Convergent neuroimmune signaling underlying rapid antidepressant response to ketamine and psychedelics.
articles.abstract: Despite distinct receptor targets, both ketamine and serotonergic psychedelics produce a rapid clinical response and share biological signatures that suggest convergence on common downstream molecular mediators. To identify shared biomarkers of rapid antidepressant response, this study integrated CSF proteomics from healthy volunteers (HVs) who received intravenous ketamine with transcriptomic analyses from induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) derived from participants with treatment-resistant depression (TRD) and HVs; iPSCs were treated with ketamine, its metabolite (2 R,6 R)-hydroxynorketamine, lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), or psilocybin. Multimodal clinical characterization (transcriptomics (n = 16 TRD; 11 HV), magnetoencephalography (MEG) (n = 30 TRD; 25 HV), and plasma cytokines (n = 39 TRD; 25 HV) were also performed on TRD and HV participants who received a single dose of intravenous ketamine (0.5 mg/kg) or placebo. Conserved immune pathways were identified across CSF and iPSC neurons with interleukin-15 (IL)-15 and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) emerging as key regulatory hubs. Transcriptomically, in whole blood, ketamine responders exhibited decreased IL-15 and elevated B-cell signaling pathways at baseline that were reversed post-treatment. At the protein level, plasma IL-7 levels (primary B-cell driver) correlated with baseline MEG gamma power, reaching brain-wide significance across all participants (main effect pFDR < 0.05). The association was most pronounced in the TRD participants across subcortical regions (diagnosis x IL-7 pFDR < 10-14). Post-ketamine, the TRD IL-7-gamma relationship inverted, paralleling widespread gamma power reductions throughout default-mode network regions (session x IL-7 pclc < 0.05). In mixed-effects models, cytokine ratios linked to IL-7/IL-15 signaling predicted antidepressant response (IL-4/interferon gamma (IFN-γ) pFDR < 0.041) and non-response (MCP-1/IL-7 pFDR < 0.009), suggesting that rebalancing within the IL-7/IL-15 axis may contribute to therapeutic efficacy. Clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT00088699; NCT02484456.

articles.title: Chitosan-based nanocarriers in Alzheimer's disease therapy: recent developments and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurological condition that worsens with time and causes behavioural problems, memory loss, and cognitive decline. It is a major global health concern. Alzheimer's complexity and the blood-brain barrier (BBB) limit effective disease-modifying treatments despite extensive research. The primary goal of conventional pharmacotherapies is to relieve symptoms; however, they frequently have low absorption, a short half-life, and peripheral adverse effects. The use of anti-Alzheimer medications in nanoparticles (NPs) is a potential remedy for these issues. Although many NPs are biocompatible and non-toxic, many are not biodegradable, making them unsuitable for CNS targeting. Chitosan (CS)-based NPs stand out among polymeric nanocarriers as stable, biodegradable delivery systems for central nervous system drugs. In this review, we examine the design, mechanisms of BBB penetration, drug-loading capacity, controlled-release behaviour, and therapeutic efficacy of CS-based delivery platforms, including nanoparticles, nanogels, lipid nanoparticles, polymeric micelles, nanoemulsions, and acetylcholinesterase inhibitor-loaded systems. Furthermore, the benefits of CS-based systems, including improved brain bioavailability, reduced toxicity, intranasal delivery, and support for multifunctional and stimuli-responsive therapeutics, are highlighted. All things considered, chitosan-based drug delivery systems offer a flexible and promising strategy for enhancing AD treatment results.

articles.title: Synovial Biomarker Modulation and Clinical Response to Umbilical Cord-Derived MSC Treatment in Knee Osteoarthritis: A Case Series Study.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveUmbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (UC-MSCs) are a promising treatment for knee osteoarthritis (KOA). This study aimed to (1) characterize early synovial fluid biomarker changes after intra-articular UC-MSCs therapy in advanced KOA and (2) explore their relationship with short-term clinical outcomes.MethodsIn this prospective, single-arm case series, 15 patients with advanced KOA (Kellgren-Lawrence III-IV) scheduled for total knee arthroplasty received a single intra-articular injection of 20 × 106 allogeneic UC-MSCs. Synovial fluid was aspirated at baseline and approximately 6 weeks post-injection. A panel of 29 soluble biomarkers related to inflammation, matrix remodeling, immune signaling, angiogenesis, and metabolism was quantified using multiplex immunoassays. Clinical status was evaluated with Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) before and at a mean of 48 ± 18 days after the injection. Paired differences were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.ResultsSignificant post-treatment differences were observed in biomarkers associated with extracellular matrix turnover (Matrix Metalloproteinase [MMP]-1, MMP-3, MMP-7, Cartilage Oligomeric Matrix Protein [COMP]), vascular remodeling (Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor [VEGF], Vascular Cell Adhesion Molecule [VCAM]-1), immune modulation (interleukin [IL]-8), and metabolic or structural regulation (Leptin, dickkopf [Dkk]-1). Most PROMs demonstrated significant improvements. These findings describe molecular changes in synovial fluid observed after intra-articular UC-MSC administration.ConclusionsIn this prospective single-arm cohort, intra-articular UC-MSC administration was feasible and well tolerated, and we observed pre-post changes in synovial fluid biomarkers and patient-reported outcomes. These findings do not establish causality and warrant confirmation in controlled studies. The study was registered at Clinicaltrials.gov: Mechanisms of Treatment Effects Using Cultured, Allogeneic Mesenchymal Stromal Stem Cells (MSCs) in Knee Osteoarthritis, NCT06078059, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06078059?intr=NCT06078059.

articles.title: Neurorehabilitation as an Opportunity for Structured Post-Stroke Lipid Management: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Background and PurposeIschemic stroke remains a major cause of death, disability, and recurrent vascular events worldwide. Although lipid-lowering therapy is central to secondary prevention, the transition between acute stroke care and long-term outpatient management remains a vulnerable period during which guideline-directed treatment is frequently delayed, undertitrated, or discontinued. Neurorehabilitation may provide an important opportunity to address this gap. This narrative review summarizes evidence supporting intensive low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction after ischemic stroke and examines how the neurorehabilitation setting may facilitate optimized lipid management.MethodsA literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through March 2026, combining terms across three domains: (1) ischemic stroke and secondary prevention, (2) lipid-lowering therapy, and (3) neurorehabilitation and functional recovery. Included study types encompassed randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews with meta-analyses, clinical practice guidelines, observational cohort and preclinical studies addressing statin pleiotropic effects. Priority was given to landmark randomized trials, major society guidelines, and studies with direct relevance to recurrent stroke prevention, hemorrhagic risk stratification, and rehabilitation-based care delivery.ResultsEvidence from SPARCL, Treat Stroke to Target, FOURIER, and Ez PAVE shows that intensive LDL-C reduction improves secondary stroke prevention. Statins may also affect neuroinflammation, endothelial function, blood-brain barrier integrity, and neuroplasticity, with differences in hemorrhagic stroke risk and safety profiles compared with PCSK9 inhibitors.ConclusionAlthough direct rehabilitation-based randomized trials are lacking, integrating supervised medication titration, adherence monitoring, neuroimaging-guided risk stratification, and patient-centered secondary prevention strategies into neurorehabilitation may represent a practical approach for strengthening secondary stroke prevention and reducing recurrent vascular events.

articles.title: The dual role of microglia in cognitive dysfunction: from neuroinflammation to therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Cognitive dysfunction is a major global burden. Microglia mediate neuroinflammation linking diverse etiologies to neuronal injury, with their functions extending beyond the brain parenchyma to include bidirectional crosstalk with the neurovascular unit. This review examines the dual role of microglia in cognitive disorders and therapeutic implications of their plasticity. Modern transcriptomic studies indicate that microglial states are multidimensional and context-dependent, rather than conforming to a simple M1/M2 dichotomy. Instead, microglia exist along a dynamic continuum encompassing homeostatic, disease-associated, and senescence-associated states. The relative contribution of protective and detrimental programs changes according to disease stage, anatomical location, pathological burden, and local cellular environment, and the two programs may coexist even within the same disease stage. Therapeutic strategies are therefore shifting from broad anti-inflammatory suppression toward precision modulation of microglial states. Their translational readiness varies from preclinical proof-of-concept to Phase II/III evaluation, and target engagement alone does not ensure restoration of physiological microglial function or cognitive benefit. Emerging interventions include TREM2 agonists, CSF1R modulators, PPARγ activators, NLRP3/STING/complement inhibitors, and microglia replacement. Key challenges include brain-targeted delivery and biomarker validation. Understanding microglia as plastic, context-dependent regulators may inform precision immunomodulatory therapies.

articles.title: Bilirubin in depression: redox-inflammatory mechanisms, clinical associations, and biomarker potential.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a heterogeneous psychiatric disorder associated with oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroendocrine dysregulation, and altered neuroplasticity. Bilirubin, an endogenous heme metabolite, exhibits antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties in experimental systems, suggesting potential relevance to biological pathways implicated in depression. This review critically examines the biological rationale and clinical evidence linking bilirubin with depression and evaluates its potential translational significance. Clinical studies report heterogeneous associations between bilirubin concentrations and depressive outcomes across different populations, including MDD, postpartum depression, post-stroke depression, and individuals with diabetes. Some studies suggest inverse or potentially nonlinear associations, while findings vary according to population characteristics and clinical context. These observations may reflect differences in metabolic status, liver function, medication exposure, genetic variation, and other confounding factors. Proposed mechanisms involve oxidative and inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial function, neuroendocrine regulation, and vascular pathways; however, much of the mechanistic evidence derives from experimental models or populations other than individuals with MDD. Observational associations and experimental antioxidant effects do not establish that bilirubin causally protects against depression. Current evidence does not establish bilirubin as a validated diagnostic or prognostic biomarker for depression or as a causal protective factor. Bilirubin may warrant investigation as an adjunct within multimarker approaches, but its incremental clinical value remains uncertain. Larger longitudinal, multicenter, mechanistic, and multi-omics studies using standardized measurement methods are needed to clarify temporal and causal relationships, assess population-specific associations, and determine whether bilirubin contributes meaningfully to risk stratification or treatment monitoring.

articles.title: Glioblastoma-associated microglia/macrophages (GAMs): Advances in knowledge and implications for glioblastoma (GBM) therapy.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an exceptionally aggressive, therapy-resistant central nervous system malignancy. Within the tumour microenvironment, glioblastoma-associated microglia and macrophages (GAMs) constitute a highly heterogeneous population whose functional states profoundly influence disease progression, tissue architecture, immune evasion, and treatment response. In this review, we propose a conceptual framework in which distinct GAM phenotypes emerge from the integrated influence of vascular, tumoural, metabolic, biomechanical, neural, and immune inputs, together with glyco-immune interactions, extracellular vesicles, and epigenetic regulation. As GAMs process these cues, they actively remodel their surrounding ecosystem, sustaining a protumourigenic niche. We critically evaluate emerging therapeutic interventions-including those targeting GAM abundance, immunometabolism, mechanotransduction, and intercellular communication-as well as advanced platforms such as engineered myeloid systems, phytomedicines, targeted delivery vehicles, and gut-brain axis-based strategies. Furthermore, we address key translational bottlenecks, including extreme GAM plasticity, spatial heterogeneity, limitations of preclinical models, barriers to central nervous system delivery, and a lack of predictive biomarkers. We argue that the therapeutically relevant target is not the GAM population in isolation, but rather the diverse niche-GAM functional units and the cumulative signalling networks that sustain them. Ultimately, achieving durable clinical efficacy will require biomarker-guided, spatially informed combination regimens that selectively disrupt maladaptive myeloid states while preserving physiological microglial homeostasis.

articles.title: Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity as Multicellular Network Failure: Cardiac Niche Reprogramming and Pathological Cell-Cell Communication.
articles.abstract: Anthracyclines are essential anticancer agents, yet a cardiomyocyte-centered model incompletely explains why cardiac injury can be delayed, progressive, and poorly captured by resting ejection fraction. We frame anthracycline cardiotoxicity as a multicellular network failure within the cardiac niche: the spatially organized interactions among cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial and immune cells, extracellular matrix, and circulating signals. Cardiomyocyte stress initiates injury, whereas pathological communication may propagate it. We distinguish a fibroblast-CD8+ T-cell adhesion circuit, supported by loss-of-function evidence in mice and correlative human data, from an emerging therapy-conditioned tumor-heart extracellular vesicle axis supported mainly by breast cancer models. These pathways may converge on fibrotic stiffness, microvascular dysfunction, and electrical uncoupling; however, direct cross-circuit interaction and drug-independent sufficiency remain unproven. We integrate established clinical risk modifiers with this framework, specify causal criteria, and propose spatial multiomics, living myocardial slices, tumor-bearing systems, and longitudinal phenotyping to test circuit persistence. This evidence-calibrated model shifts the goal from cataloging cell-intrinsic pathways to identifying mechanism-resolved biomarkers and therapeutically targetable communication nodes while preserving antitumor efficacy.

articles.title: Nanoparticle-Mediated Therapies for Atherosclerosis: A Novel Approach to Targeted Treatment.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atherosclerosis(AS) remains a leading cause of global cardiovascular mortality due to the formation of lipid rich plaques and chronic vascular inflammation. Conventional therapies, including statins, antiplatelet agents and surgical interventions, primarily control risk factors by preventing new plaque deposits but show limited ability to selectively target inflamed vascular sites.
OBJECTIVE: This review critically evaluates current advances in nanoparticle mediated drug delivery for atherosclerosis, with emphasis on mechanistic targeting of inflamed plaques, modulation of macrophage driven inflammatory and oxidative pathways within the diseased vascular microenvironment. This review also highlights comparative analysis of major nanoparticle systems, integration of theranostic functionalities for simultaneous molecular imaging and therapy. The translational barriers are also addressed to enable clinical implementation.Significance of Review: Despite advancements in lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory drugs, current atherosclerosis treatments are limited by inadequate plaque specificity, rapid systemic clearance, off-target toxicity, and persistent cardiovascular risk. Nanoparticle based systems can solve these problems with simultaneous diagnosis and therapy, thereby addressing major unmet clinical needs.Key Findings: Different types of nanoparticles demonstrate promising therapeutic outcomes by modulating macrophage activity, reducing oxidative stress, enabling controlled drug release and improving plaque imaging. Theranostic nanoparticles further allow simultaneous diagnosis and treatment. However, large-scale manufacturing, nanotoxicology and regulatory constraints continue to hinder clinical translation.
CONCLUSIONS: Nanoparticle-mediated therapies represent a transformative approach for atherosclerosis by enabling precision, targeted and multifunctional treatment. Continued optimization of safety, scalability and regulatory compliance will be essential for successful clinical adoption and improved patient outcomes.
